ORAL ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Hike in security deposit for new LPG connections 
*401. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that the public sector oil 
companies such as Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and 
Hindustan Petroleum have stopped issuing new LPG connections; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether it is a fact that the oil companies have demanded a 
security deposit hike of Rs. 250/- for each new connection after the cost 
of steel went up from Rs. 17000 per ton to Rs. 28000 per ton; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) what is Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI 
MANI SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) to (e) AStatement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The release of new c onnections by Public Sector Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs) has been affected by shortage of cylinders 
due to cylinder manufacturers not honouring their commitment on 
supplies because of continuous increase in steel prices. This has resulted 
in some build-up of waiting lists of  new customers. Government have, 
therefore, directed OMCs to liquidate by mid-September the waiting list 
of LPG customers as on 1.8.2004. 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
(c) to (e) OMCs have approached the Government for an increase 
in security deposit for LPG cylinders due to hike in procurement cost 
of cylinders following increase in steel prices. The matter is under 
consideration of the Government.

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Assistance to panchayats due to flood 
† *403. SHRI VIDYASAGAR NISHAD: Will the Minister of 
WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that several panchayats of Gogri-
block of Khagaria in Bihar have been affected due to flood; and 
(b) what assistance has been provided by the Central Government 
to the affected panchayats so far and the steps being taken to construct 
platforms with roofs in the said panchayats? 
†The Original notice of question was received in Hindi. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYA RANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) Yes, Sir. As reported by the State Government of Bihar, 
several panchayats of Gogri-block of Khagaria district in Bihar have been 
affected by floods in July, 2004. 
(b) Flood Management being a State subject, it is the primary 
responsibility of the State Governm ent concerned for the execution of 
rescue and relief operations. The Government of India supplements the 
efforts of the State Governments, where necessary, by extending financial 
and logistic support as per the pr ovisions of the Eleventh Finance 
Commission. For this purpose, the Finance Commission has allocated 
certain amount under Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) to each State. 
Assistance for calamity of severe nature is also provided from National 
Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF) after following the laid down procedure. 
During the current year 2004-05, besides releasing Rs.90.12 crore under 
CRF, an amount of Rs. 55 crore has been provided to the State Government 
from NCCF. 
Providing relief at the ground level comes within the purview of the 
State Government. Further, the State Government has informed that 
presently there is no such scheme either under execution or envisaged 
for construction of platforms with roofs. However, the Government of 
India has constituted a Task Force to look into the problem of recurring 
floods in various States including Bihar.

Rural and urban share in bank deposits 
*405. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the rural and urban share in bank deposits, at present; 
(b) the amount of loans provided by banks in rural areas; 
(c) whether Government propose to provide more loans for rural 
areas; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) 
and (b) The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported that the share of 
rural, semi-urban and urban (including Metropolitan) areas in banks' 
deposits during the year 2003- 04 was 12.86%, 17.62% and 69.52%, 
respectively. The bank credit given to the rural areas during the said 
period was Rs. 85,224 crores (approx) representing 9.56% of the total 
credit. 
(c) and (d) Pursuant to the Agriculture Credit Policy announced by 
Government on June 18, 2004, the RBI has advised all Scheduled 
Commercial Banks and NABARD to all Cooperative Banks to enhance 
agricultural credit during the year 2004-05. Keeping in view the 
Government's goal of significantly improving flow of credit and covering 
additional farmers under institutional credit, the aforesaid policy envisages 
the following measures:— 
(i) Rescheduling/restructuring loans of distressed farmers; 
(ii) One Time Settlement (OTS) for small and marginal farmers; 
(iii) Fresh finance for farmers whose earlier debts have been settled 
through compromise or write off; and 
(iv) Relief measures for farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders. 
The RBI and NABARD have issued guidelines in this behalf, on 24th 
June and 29th June 2004, respectively to Schedule Commercial Banks 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
and Cooperatives. The Credit flow to Agriculture from all lending institutions 
is projected at about Rs. 1,05,000 crores. 
The above policy envisages coverage of at least 100 new farmers at 
each rural and semi-urban branch, targeting a total number of 50 lakh 
farmers throughout the country; loans for two to three investment projects 
in the new areas of plantation and horticulture, fisheries, organic farming, 
agro-processing, livestock, micro irrigation, sprinkler irrigation, watershed 
management, village ponds development and other allied activities, apart 
from financing 10 agro-clinics in every district. 
Committee for proper water management 
†*406. DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: 
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have constituted a new Committee for 
suggesting proper management of water in the country; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and by when the said Committee is 
likely to submit its report; 
(c) whether Government had received suggestions with regard to 
proper management of water during the past years also; and 
(d) if so, the action taken thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYA RANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) to (d) The Government has not constituted any new 
Committee for suggesting proper management of water in the country. 
However, Ministry of Water Resources has constituted a Task Force for 
Flood Management/Erosion Control to suggest short term and long term 
measure for management of flood control in Assam and other 
neighbouring states as well as Bi har, West Bengal and Eastern Uttar 
Pradesh. The Planning Commission has also constituted (i) Task Group 
on Integration of ongoing schemes to address Water Conservation as a 
Water Mission and (ii) Task Group on Efficient utilisation of Water 
Resources. 
The suggestions on various issues relating to development and 
management of water resources are expressed by experts from time to

Farmer-friendly Credit Policy 
*407. SHRI B. J. PANDA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government propose to bring in a farmer-
friendly credit policy during the current fiscal; 
(b) if so, the details of the proposed scheme; 
(c) whether Government would grant interest-free loans to certain 
categories of poor farmers; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) what is the action plan of Government to control suicides by 
debt-ridden farmers in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (S HRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) 
and (b) An announcement has already been made by the Government 
on 18.6.2004 for increasing the ground level credit flow to agriculture 
and allied activities by 30% during 2004-05 and doubling the flow in 
three years. This Farmer-Friendl y Agriculture Credit Package also 
envisages debt restructuring/resched uling and fresh loans to farmers 
affected by natural calamities, One Time Settlement (OTS) for small 
and marginal farmers, fresh finance for farmers whose earlier debts 
have been settled through compromise or write off and relief measures 
for farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders. 
Pursuant to the above announcement, Reserve Bank of India has 
already advised all scheduled commercial banks on 24.6.2004 to take 
action to implement the programme. National Bank for Agriculture and 
Rural Development (NABARD) has also issued similar guidelines to 
Regional Rural Banks and cooperatives. 
(c) and (d) The announcement does not envisage providing interest 
free loans to farmers. 
(e) In order to provide relief to farmers facing actue distress due to 
their heavy indebtedness to non-institutional lenders i.e. money lenders, 
banks have been advised to give loans to such farmers against 
appropriate collateral or groups security.

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to 
(c) RBI has reported that the inspection reports conducted under Section 
35 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 of banks are confidential in nature 
and hence, contents of these reports cannot be disclosed as per 
provisions of Section 34-A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI), on the directions of its Board for 
Financial Supervision (BFS), has prescribed a procedure for dealing 
with divergence in assessment of non-performing assets as assessed 
by the bank and certified by the Statutory Auditors and as assessed by 
the Principal Inspecting Officers (PIO) of the RBI. Divergence is grouped 
into two headings viz. subjective and objective criteria. When the additional 
provision recommended by Principal Inspecting Officer exceeds 5% to 
the total provisions held in case of divergence arising out of objective 
parameters, or 15% to total provisions held in case of divergence arising 
out of subjective criteria, the same are termed as "significant", and the 
same are re-examined independently by another senior officer of the bank. 
In case of continued divergence, the Statutory Auditors/Management of 
the banks would have to ensure that the shortfall in the provision is made 
good in the next financial year. 
The ICICI Bank Ltd. has reported in its published documents, the gross 
NPAs at Rs. 5013.03 crore as on March 31, 2002, Rs. 5027.38 crore as on

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYA RANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) and (b) A long-term analysis of ground water levels by 
the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), under the Ministry of Water 
Resources during the years 1983—2002 indicates decline in ground water 
levels by more than 4 meters in parts of some districts of various States 
of the country. The names of the States/districts having pockets of 
declining water level in the last twenty years (1983—2002) are given in 
the Statement (see below) 
(c) In order to check receding of ground water level, the following 
measures have been suggested:— 
(i) Ground water resources augmentation through rain water 
harveting and artificial recharge to ground water. 
(ii) Regulation of ground water development through notification 
and legislation. 
(d) Water being a State subject, it is primarily the responsibility of 
the concerned State Governments to plan, finance and execute schemes 
for augmenting water resources. The Central Government has initiated 
18 

[24 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
following measures to check over-exploitation of ground water:— 
(i) Implementation of a Central Sector Scheme for Study of Recharge 
to Ground Water in the country. 
(ii) Circulation of Manual/Guidelines on Artificial Recharge of Ground 
Water to the States/Union Territories to enable them to formulate 
area specific artificial recharge schemes to check the declining 
trend of ground water levels. 
(iii) Circulation of a Model Bill in the year 1970 which was re-circulated 
in 1992 and again in 1996 to all the States/Union Territories to 
enable them to enact suitable legislation for regulation and control 
of ground water development. 
(iv) Organisation of 187 mass awareness programmes and 118 
training courses on rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge of 
ground water. 
(v) Constitution of Central Ground Water Authority under the

Telecommunications, Central Public Works Department and

(c) if so, whether the Central Government have drawn up some action

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYARANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) Yes, Sir. As per Ministry of Rural Development, an area 
of 26,178 Sq. Km. in 8 districts covering 47 Blocks in Orissa is covered 
under Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP). 
(b) to (d) Water being a State subject, all water resources schemes 
including the schemes meant for drought proofing of drought prone areas 
in the country are planned, formulated, implemented and funded by the 
respective State Governments out of their own resources and as per 
their own priorities. However, with  an objective to accelerate the 
implementation of those projects which are beyond resource capability 
of the States or are in advanced stage of completion, Central Government 
launched an Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) during 
1996-97 to provide Central Loan Assistance (CLA) on matching basis to 
major/medium projects in the country. Priorities are given to those projects 
which are benefiting Tribal and Drought Prone Areas. Since 1999-2000, 
CLA has been provided in the ratio of 3:1 (Centre : State) to Special 
Category States including KBK Districts of Orissa i.e. Kalahandi, Bolangir, 
Naupada and Sonepur, and in the rati o of 2:1 (Centre : State) for the 
projects in rest of the Orissa State. 
With effect from February 2002, AIBP has been linked to economic 
eforms in the irrigation sector and the guidelines have been modified 
accordingly. Since then CLA is being provided to the Reforming States 
under General Category in the ratio of 4:1 (Centre : State) and in the 
ratio of 1:0) (Centre: State) under special category including KBK Districts 
of Orissa, in case they rationalize their water rates in such a way as to 
recover full O & M cost of irrigation projects in 5 years. The State of 
Orissa have been included under the Category of Reforming States. 
So far CLA amounting to Rs. 898.250 crore has been released to 
Government of Orissa. In all, 17 major/medium and 23 Surface Minor 
Irrigation (Ml) Schemes of Orissa have received CLA under AIBP. Out of 
the 17 major/medium irrigation projects, 8 projects are in KBK Districts. 
These 8 projects and 23 Surface Water Ml Schemes have received CLAof

In order to bridge the gap between potential created and that utilized

Bank?

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) and (b) Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

directions since 4th June, 2004 under section 35A of Banking Regulation Act,

prevent preferential treatment, which was required to protect the interest of the

irregularities and deficiencies of the bank. In view of this, the 
Commissioner of Co-operation and-Registrar of Co-operative Societies 
(RCS), Maharashtra was requisitioned to supersede the Board of Directors 
in May, 2004. The Board was superseded and Administrator was appointed on 
June 5,2004. The RCS was advised on 2.6.2004 to fix accountability in respect

affairs of the bank and take appropriate action.

agriculture, particularly irrigation and infrastructure to reinforce the 
campaign against poverty and unemployment;

revenue deficit, coupled with substantial decrease in domestic savings due

GDP for enhanced public investment without undermining fiscal prudence.

education and health, and facilitating their full participation in the growth process,

eliminating poverty and unemployment. It will also reinforce the growth process,

2143. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) what are the reasons for the difference between the lending rates of 
public sector banks and private sector banks; 
(b) whether the difference between minimum and maximum interest 
rates for demand loans has widened; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) The lending rates of scheduled 
commercial banks have been deregulated by RBI since October, 1994, 
subject to the condition that banks have to declare their Prime Lending Rates 
(PLRs), as approved by their Boards. For credit limits up to Rs. 2 lakh, 
PLR remains the ceiling rate. The PLR is generally fixed by the banks 
taking into account inter-alia, their cost of funds, operational cost, risk 
capital requirements etc. Since April 2001, commericalbanks have been 
given freedom to lend at sub-PLR rates tocreditworthy borrowers on the 
basis of a transparent and objective policy approved by their Boards. 
(b) and (c) RBI has reported that the spread between the maximum and 
minimum lending rates widened between March 2003 and March 2004, 
although there is a general decline in lending rates, both for demand and term 
loans. However, the decline is sharper for public sector banks (PSBs) vis-a-vis 
private sector banks. The range of lending rates for various banks groups for

Waiver of interest on crop loans 
2145. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the decision of Government regarding waiver of interest to farmers 
on their kharif 2002 crop loans and full re-imbursement thereof by the 
Central Government, as announced earlier in view of wide-spread drought 
and in view of NABARD not implement ing Government assurances of 
total waiver of interest specially in Andhra Pradesh; and 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) and (b) Considering the severe 
drought during the Kharif 2002, Hon'ble Prime Minister announced in 
the parliament on 18th December, 2002 to convert the short term Kharif 
crop loan, 2002 along with its interest into 4/5 years term loan and to 
waive of first year deferred liability of interest subject to a maximum of 
20% of total interest as a one-time measure to mitigate the hardship 
of drought affected farmers. AS a follow up, RBI vide their circular 
dated 27th December, 2002 advised all scheduled commerical banks 
83 

RAJYA SABHA [24 A ugust, 2004] 
accordingly and NABARD did the same for Regional Rural Banks and 
Cooperative Banks. 
NABARD has already reimbursed Rs. 9.92 crore towards the interest 
waived by 14 Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) in the State of Andhra 
Pradesh under the scheme announced by the Government of India. As 
regards Cooperatives, the State Government of Andhra Pradesh had its 
own scheme to waive of 100% interest on Kharif 2002 crop loans, 
provided the farmers repay the pr incipal. Since the scheme envisaged 
repayment of principal, the Cooperative Banks had not extended term loan 
conversion facility to the farmers and hence were not eligible for 
reimbursement of even the first year  deferred interest liability waived 
by them.

Revised inspection system for Banks 
2155. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: Will the Minister of FINANCE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Reserve Bank of India proposes to 
implement the revised inspection system for banks after shifting to the Risk 
Based Supervision (RBS) system; 
93 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
(b) whether in the proposed RBS system, the supervisory tools will focus 
on greater off site surveillance and targeted on-site inspections; and 
(c) if so, the advantages of revised inspection system? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. As per 
announcement made by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in its monetary and 
credit policy statement for 2000-01, RBI has developed an overall plan for 
monitoring towards Risk Based Supervision (RBS). The basic tool for 
RBS system would be risk profile templates prepared by the banks and 
vetted by RBI. The risks are segregated into eight inherent business risks 
and four control risks, based on the risk matrix of individual bank. RBS 
will focus on targeted on-site inspections depending upon the overall risk 
of individual risk parameters of the said bank, level of risk etc. In addition 
to targeted on-site monitoring, banks are subjected to continuous 
monitoring through off-site surveillance mechanism. 
(c) RBS would benefit the supervisor (RBI) and the supervised entities 
(banks). The adoption of RBS would lead to deeper understanding of the 
risks faced by banks and thereby, facilitate optimum use of scarce 
supervisory resources and direct s upervisory attention to those banks 
and those areas within the banks, which cause more supervisory concern. 
RBS ensure prompt compliance with the regulatory and supervisory 
requirements of RBI. It would also be nefit banks in two ways, first, it 
would enhance the bank's own capability for risk management and risk 
control and second, it will provide a built in incentive of lesser supervisory 
intervention for the good performer.

Home loan fraud cases 
2172. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of 
FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether several home loan frauds have been reported in banks 
recently; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps taken to co-ordinate among all banks and registrar's 
office to counter the menace of frauds in home loans? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) According to the information furnished by the Reserve Bank of 
India, the details of fraud in home loans involving amount of Rs. One crore 
111 

RAJYA SABHA [24 A ugust, 2004] 
and above during the last three years are as under: 
 
Calender Year No. of frauds Amount in crore 
2002 3 8.24 
2003 7 35.34 
2004 (up to June) 1 5.81 
The modus operandi observed in the fraud cases involved one or 
more of the following methods- 
• The same property was offered as security to different banks by 
submitting fake title deeds. 
• The properties, which were mortgaged to the banks, were found 
to be fictitious/non existent. 
• Loans were granted to persons without verifying their whereabouts/ 
details. Such persons were subsequently found to be non-existent. 
• The documents such as title deeds, income tax returns, salary 
certificates etc. submitted for availing the loans were found to be 
fake/fictitious. 
• The Chartered Accountants who had issued/verified the documents 
were found to be fake/non-existent themselves. 
• In a number of fraud cases, the builders/developers had defrauded 
the banks by pocketing the housing loans which they managed to 
obtain in the names of fictitious persons by submitting forged 
documents. 
(c) The steps initiated by RBI to counter the menance of frauds in 
home loans are given below: 
(i) RBI requested all State Governments to computerize land records 
in the sub-Registrar's office to check/avoid multiple charges. State 
Governments were also requested for setting up a "Control 
Registry" which would enable lendi ng institutions to check the 
charges on the property/valid title on the property at the 
Government/Registration Office. 
(ii) All fraud cases involving amounts of Rupees one crore and above 
are followed up by Fraud Monitoring Cell, of RBI. Caution advices 
in respect of builders/unscrupulous borrowers availing home loans 
are issued on receipt of such fraud reports from banks. 
112 

[24 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA  
(iii) Fraud involving amounts of Rs. one lakh and above and upto Rs. one 
crore are monitored by Regional Offices of RBI. 
(iv) Frauds below Rs. one lakh are reported by commercial banks in a 
consolidated manner to RBI at quarterly intervals. 
(v) RBI has advised banks to carry out field level inspections at 
branches having large exposure in home loans. 
(vi) The bank officials are called for discussions at Department of Banking 
Supervision (DBS) of RBI on the issues relating to frauds to impress upon 
them the need for preventive steps to be taken for minimizing frauds 
in housing bans. 
(vi) Wherever necessary, the banks have also lodged complaints with 
Police/CBI/Criminal complaints in court of law in the cases of fraud to 
deter people and employees from indulging in fraudulent activities.

External debt 
2174. SHRIMATI S.G INDIRA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that in December, 2003, India's external debt 
stood at U.S. dollar 112.1 billion up by U.S. dollar 6.8 billion over the level of 
end December, 2002; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the decision to do away with two 
popular NRI schemes resulted in this increase; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether Government are considering to re-introduce Non-Resident 
(Non-repatriable) Rupee Deposit and the Non-Resident Special Rupee 
Deposit Scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI  S. S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The increase in the external debt was mainly due to the 
surge in the NRI deposits. One of the reasons for the increase in the NRI 
deposits was the discontinuation of the Non-Resident (Non-repatriable) 
Rupee Deposit [NR(N R)RD] scheme with effect from April 1,2002, which partly 
resulted in the higher inflows into the Non-Resident (External) Rupee Account 
[NR(E)RA] as the maturity proceeds of the [NR(NR)RD] were allowed to be 
credited to the [NR (E)RA]. Under the existing practice for compilation of 
external debt statistics, the deposits under the [NR(NR)RD] scheme did not form 
part of external debt, as the principal amount under the scheme was not 
repatriable. However, on discontinuation of this scheme and the subsequent 
crediting of maturity proceeds of [NR(NR)RD] deposits to the [NR(E)RA], these 
deposits are now reckoned as external debt liabilities. 
(d) No such proposal is under consideration.

class tourists; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
(SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) Yes, Sir. There is a problem of 
lack of availability of adequate confirmed seats/ berths in rail/coaches, 
airlines and accommodation for domestic tourists during the peak season. 
(b) and (c) Tour packages are structured and operated by private

effective tour packages particularly during the summer holidays are offered 
by India Tourism Development Corporation, Indian Airlines, Delhi Tourism 
and Transportation Development Corp oration Ltd., and Ministry of 
Railways:—

journey/accommodation for domestic tourists through various 
Ashok Travels & Tours (ATT) units spread across the country.

the Government on these packages.

as Indian Airlines Flyaways) which offer the facility of booking Air 
tickets, accommodation under a single window and the cost is 
reasonable. To make the packages affordable, Indian Airlines 
discounts its sector air fares by upto 25%. Also just within the 
cost of air fare, most packages include a 3 night/4 day holiday in 
a good category hotel with breakfast, airport transfer, sightseeing, 
taxes, etc.

been organising tour packages specially during summer holidays 
to various tourist places keeping in view the middle class people

are organised by non-AC luxury buses and accommodation on 
r'oom sharing basis is provided to make the packages more cost

assessed at 1869 BCM. The utilisabte water resources is assessed as 1122

well as ground water. A number of surface and ground water schemes are

Erosion crisis in West Bengal 
2238. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:  Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether erosion has emerged as a crisis in some parts of West 
Bengal, especially in the Malda-Murshidabad districts; 
(b) whether there has been any demand to declare it as a national 
calamity; and 
(c) what steps are being taken by Government to curb the problem? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYANA YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. 
There are reports of severe bank erosion in some parts of West Bengal 
including Malda and Murshidabad districts. 
(b) Yes, Sir. 
(c) Though the Flood Management including river erosion is a state 
subject, the Government of India is provding assistance to West Bengal 
to tackle this problem through a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) 
which was formulated in January, 2001 for implementing critical anti erosion 
schemes. Under this scheme, an amount of Rs. 28.66 crore has so far 
174 

[24 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
been released to West Bengal till 2003-04 for taking up anti erosion 
schemes in Malda and Murshidabad districts. The above scheme is also 
being continued further during 2004-07 for which an amount of Rs. 51.00 
crore has been earmarked for the State of West Bengal as Central share 
to take up the critical anti erosion works at an estimated cost of Rs. 
68.00 crore which interalia include seven nos. of schemes for Malda and 
Murshidabad districts. 
In addition to above Farakka Barrage Project Authorities are also 
undertaking the critical anti-erosion works in and around Farakka Barrage 
Project. Since 9th Plan, an amount of Rs. 38.74 crore has been incurred 
by the project on critical anti erosion works in Malda and Murshidabad 
districts till June, 2004. Futher, a provision of Rs. 8.1 crore has been 
made under the CSS for Farakka Barrage Project to take up anti erosion 
works on river Ganga/Padma within its jurisdiction during 2004-07 with 
100% Central funding. 
In order to look into the flood & erosion problem in Assam & 
neighbouring States as well as Bihar, West Bengal and Eastern Uttar 
Pradesh, Government of India have constituted a Task Force in August 
2004 which has been asked to submit their report in a time bound manner.

 Electrification of villages in Uttar Pradesh 
*421. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the details of villages in Uttar Pradesh where electrification is yet to be 
done; 
(b) the details of Government's rural electrification scheme: and 
(c) by when electrification work in all the villages in Uttar Pradesh will be 
done by Government? 
 
1 
 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P. M. SAYEED): (a) In Uttar 
Pradesh, there are 40080 villages yet to be electrified as on 31.03.04. 
(b) To achieve the objective of the National Common Minimum Programme 
of completing rural household electrification in five years a new strategy 
has been drawn up, which envisages: 
(i) Creation of Rural Electricity Distribution Backbone (REDB) of 33/11 KV 
substations, with at least one such substation in each block appropriately 
networked and linked to the State transmission system. 
(ii) Creation of Village Electricity  Infrastructure (VEI) by providing 
Distribution Transformers) with at l east one such transformer in every 
village. 
(iii) Rural Households Electification of unetectrified households from village 
distribution transformer(s). 
(iv) Decentralized distributed generation system for such villages where grid 
connectivity is either not feasible or not cost effective. 
(c) Uttar Pradesh has been advised to target completion of village elec 
trification by the end of the 10th Plan. 
1000 MV power plant in Maharashtra 
*422. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that NTPC had decided to set up a 1000 MW power 
plant at Mauda in Nagpur district of Maharashtra and so far about Rs. one crore 
has already been spent; 
(b) the present status of this power project and by when it is likely to be 
completed; and 
(c) the total deficit of power in Vidarbha and Marathwada regions of 
Maharashtra and what steps are proposed to be taken to meet the total demand? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P. M. SAYEED): (a) and (b) NTPC has 
identified a site for development of a 1000 MW power plant at Mauda in Nagpur 
District of Maharashtra. Works for various site specific studies 
 
2 

[25 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
such as Topographical Survey, Geo-Tech nical Investigation, Seismic Study, 
Environmental Impact Assessment Study and Make-Up; Water Study etc., for the 
project have been taken up by NTPC to examine the Techno-Eco-nomic viability 
of the project. So far, approximately Rs.21 lakhs have been spent on various 
site specific studies mentioned above. 
Government of Maharashtra (GOM) conveyed its in-principle clearance for 
availability of 50 Million Cubic Metres of Water for the project from 
Gosikhurd Irrigation Project and which is expected to be completed within three 
years, once their fund requirement is tied-up. The confirmation of funding tie-
up and time frame for assured water supply is still awaited from Maharashtra 
Government. 
Coal availability from the near by coal mines is required to be confirmed. 
Setting up of the project will be taken up depending upon the establishment of 
Techno-Economic viability of the project. 
(c) As reported by Maharashtra Stat e Electricity Board (MSEB), re-gion-
wise power demand and supply study is not carried out. The study is carried out 
for the entire MSEB system. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) have informed 
that the total peak and energy deficit of power in the State of Maharashtra during the 
period April-July, 2004 and 3,102 MW (21.3%) and 2818 Million Units (9.5%) 
respectively. 
To meet the power deficits, Maharashtra has proposed a capacity addition of 
1950 MW is in 10 th Plan in the State sector. Maha rashtra is also entitled to a 
share of 1074 MW during Tenth Plan from central projects.

THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) and (b) The Government had be en receiving requests from the 
Maharashtra powerloom industry for removal of CENVAT. In this year's 
budget the following important announcements have been made for the 
textile sector as a whole including the powerloom sector:— 
• Except for mandatory excise duty on polyester filament yarn including 
texturised yarn, synthetic and artificial fibres and synthetic and 
artificial filament yarns, the whole value addition chain has been given 
excise exemption option.

• All textile goods made of pure cotton, not containing any other textile

• Other textile goods—8%

abolished.

sector:-

Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) whereby the powerloom owner

†*436. DR. NARAYAN SINGH MANAKLAO: Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the installation and construction work of 
Mathania Solar Energy Plant in Jodhpur district of Rajasthan is pending for 
more than a decade; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) by when it is likely to be started and completed? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF TH E MINISTRY OF NON-CONVEN-
TIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) and (b) 
While the proposal for the establishment of a solar thermal power plant at 
.Mathania in the Jodhpur district of Rajasthan has been under development and 
consideration for a long-time, the final detailed project report acceptable to 
various funding agencies was submitted only in the year 1998. After techno-
economic evaluation and appraisal, the project was sanc- 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
23 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
tioned by the Government in the year 2000. The project envisaged the establishment of 
a 140 MW Integrated Solar Combined Cycle power plant with naphtha as the fuel for 
the combined cycle part. Due to a sharp increase in the prices of naphtha it was decided in 
2001 to use Re-gasified Liquid Natural Gas (R-LNG) as a fuel. The Rajasthan Renewable 
Energy Corporation (RREC), the project implementing agency, went through the 
process of pre-qualification of contractors and inviting bids for turn-key execution and 
operation and maintenance of the project. As no financial bids were received inspite of 
repeated extensions, the RREC and their consultants prepared a modified bidding process. 
The RREC negotiated with Gas Authority of India Limited for the supply of natural gas 
to the project. These factors have resulted in delay in starting construction work of 
the project. 
The Ministry has considered it essential to go in for a review of the techno-
economic viability of the project because of the following factors:— 
(i) there has been change in the fuel component of the project from naphtha to gas for 
which a 350 km. long gas pipeline will need to be laid by GAIL, 
(ii) there may be a need to revise the project cost on account of change in prices of 
imported equipment, 
(iii) there is a general lowering of domestic lending rates which may render 
foreign loans unattractive, 
(iv) the power purchase agreement with suitable guarantees from the State Government 
is yet to be signed with the distribution companies, 
(v) doubts have been cast on the project's technical viability because of the inability of 
the bidders to give performance guarantees for the integrated plant, and 
(vi) CEA is examining the calculations submitted by RREC with gas as the fuel. 
(c)    It is not feasible to indicate a completion date for the project at this stage.

Special status to Rajasthan for reform in Power Sector 
†2308. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government and other institutions have 
appreciated the various steps taken by the Government of Rajasthan for  
 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
93 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
reforms in power sector in spite of scarcity of water resources; 
(b) whether Government is formulating any plan to grant the status of special 
State to Rajasthan in view of the said fact; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) to (d) The 
Government of India has started a scheme in 2000-01 called Accelerated Power 
Development Programme (APDP) to provide systematic finance to enable State 
Electricity Boards (SEBs)/ Utilities to ta ke distribution sector reform. The 
scheme has been rechristened as Accelerated Power Development & Reforms 
Programme (APDRP) in the year 2002-03. APDRP has two components. Under 
incentive component, assistance is provided as full grant to a State equivalent to 
50% of the reduction in operating cash tosses of power utility(ies). Agrant of Rs. 
137.71 crores has been released to Rajasthan as incentive during 2003-04 under 
APDRP. 
Under investment component of the APDRP, which is for assisting States in 
improving distribution network, special consideration has been accorded to Special 
Category States namely all the North Eastern States, Sikkim, Uttaranchal, 
Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. These States get APDRP assistance 
in the form of 90% grant and 10% loan. Remaining States get the assistance in 
the ratio of grant and loan on 1:1 basis. Rajasthan is covered under Non-Special 
Category States. 
The Special Category States covered under APDRP are those States which 
have been recognized as Special Category States by the National Development 
Council.

2317. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state:

electricity generation in the country; and 
(b) if so, the measures Government propose to take to meet contingencies like 
this and augment power generation? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) Generation 
from hydro power stations is dependent upon the pattern of rainfall in the 
catchment areas and reservoir level/inflows in the reservoirs of reservoir based 
hydro power stations. This year, due to inadequate rainfall, generation from hydro 
power stations has been affected. As against (generation target of 33,737 MUs 
for the period 1st April, 2004 to 17th August, 2004, hydel generation has been 
33,001 MUs representing a shortfall of 736 MUs ( i.e. 2.2%). The shortfall in 
hydel generation during the period 1s t April to 17th A ugust, 2004 accounts 
for meager 0.33% of the overall generation target during this period. 
(b) The following steps are being taken to boost the generation to make up the 
loss in hydel generation: 
(i) Postponement of planned maintenance of thermal generating units. 
(ii) Bringing back the thermal generating units already taken under planned 
shutdown on war footing. 
(iii) Increase in generation from existing thermal units. 
(iv) Close monitoring for ensuring supply of adequate coal to the power plants. 
(v) Maximization of generation from gas/liquid fuel plants. 
(vi) Ensuring maximum transfer of power from surplus regions/States to deficit 
regions/States.

Drinking water programmes 
†2346. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDELWAL: Will the Mjnister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the programmes formulated by Government for providing safe 
potable water; 
(b) what is 'Sampurna Swachchhta Abhiyan' and how does it reach the 
villages; and 
(c) the number of NGOs involved in the said programme in M.P. and the details 
thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI A. NARENDRA): (a) Water supply is a State 
subject. State Governments are primarily responsible for provinding drinking water 
facilities to rural habitations. Government of India supplement the efforts of 
the States in providing drinking water facilities to the rural habitations 
through a Centrally Spon sored Scheme namely "A ccelerated Rural Water 
Supply Programme (ARWSP)." Annual allocations made under ARWSP are 
utilized for different purposes, namely, rural water supply schemes, community 
based rural water supply schemes like Swajaldhara and Sector Reform Projects, 
water quality mitigation schemes, sustainability related projects and calamity 
relief etc. 
(b) 'Sampurna Swachchhta Abhiyan' or Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC)' is a 
programme launched to improve the ru ral sanitation coverage with active 
participation of the community. It is a demand driven programme for generating 
demand for basic sanitation facilities in household, schools, community and 
public places by creating awareness of and bringing attitudinal changes for 
relevant sanitation and hygiene practices. TSC is sanctioned taking district as a 
unit and Central funds are released to the district implementing agency which 
could be Zilla Parishad, District Rural Development Agency or District Water 
and Sanitation Mission, who in turn releases funds to villages. 
(c) NGOs play a significant role for taking up information, education, 
communication, capacity development activities and social mobilization at 
district and village levels. The engagement of NGOs is done by district 
implementing agencies only. Details of NGOs engaged by district

level. 
Wages paid to labourers under PMGSY 
†2347. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:  Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the wages paid to the labourers working on roads being constructed 
under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana; 
(b) whether these wages are uniform in all the States of the 
country; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) to (d) Rural roads is 
a State subject and funds under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) 
are released to State Government agencies for construction of rural roads. 
Contracts for construction are entered into by State Government agencies. The 
Standard Bidding Document prescribed under the PMGSY provides that the 
contractor is to pay not less than the minimum wages as per the provisions of 
Minimum Wages Act, 1948. The Act empowers the State Governments to fix 
the minimum wages. There is no requirement that the wages sould be uniform 
in all the States.

(a) whether Government are contemplating to redefine the Below Poverty Line 
(BPL) in terms of parameters of land, housing, clothing, education, health and 
sanitation besides the earlier parameters, i.e. level of calories consumption; and 
(b) if so, the details of proposed new parameters to redefine BPL people in 
urban and rural areas, separately?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) and (b) The official 
estimation of poverty is done by the Planning Commission, based on the 
Quinquennial Consumer Expenditure Survey conducted by the National Sample 
Survey Organization (NSSO). The official poverty line is anchored on the per 
capita monthly expenditure corresponding to per capita daily calorie 
requirement of 2400 in rural areas and 2100 in urban areas. The poverty line 
defined in this way covers not only the expenditure on food but also on non-food 
items such as clothing, housing, health and education and social services. The 
Government are not contemplating to redefine the poverty line so far as the 
Ministry of Rural Development is concerned.

(a) whether it is a fact that Govern ment is implementing a scheme called 
"Swarnjayanti Swarozgar Yojana' for increasing the agricultural

productivity through optimum utilization of locally available resources and 
for the welfare of women and other socially challenged sections; 
(b) if so, the details thereof with the amount released since inception of the

(c) whether it is a fact that assistance sought by Karnataka Government for 
implementation of the scheme inTumkur District (Karnataka) has so far not been 
released; and 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the likely date by when the amount will be 
released? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MATISURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) and (b) Ascheme 
captioned Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) is being 
implemented by the Government with effect from 1.4.1999. The objective of 
SGSY is to bring the assisted poor families (Swarozgaris) above the poverty 
line by ensuring appreciable increase in incomes over a period of time. This 
objective is to be achieved inter-alia by organizing, the rural poor into Self 
Help Groups (SHGs) through a process of social mobilization, their training and 
capacity building and provision of income-generating assets through a mix of 
bank credit and Government subsidy. The selection of activities under the scheme is 
based on the local resources, the aptitude and skill of the intended Swarozgaris 
and market potential for products. The scheme focuses on vulnerable section of 
the society including women and socially challenged sections. As per guidelines 
of the scheme, 50% of the group formed in each block should be exclusively 
for the women. Further, women, SCs/STs and disabled are to account for at 
least 40%, 50% and 3% of the assisted swarozgaris respectively. The amount 
released by Government of India since inception of the scheme, year-wise and 
State-wise is given in the enclosed Statement (See below). 
(c) and (d) Since inception of the scheme, the Government of India has released 
to Tumkur District in Karnataka State its due share amounting to Rs. 834.77

Recommendations of the National Commission on Youth 
†2369. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will th e Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had set up a National Commission in 
March 2002, keeping in view the problem being faced by unemployed youth and 
the report of the Commission was scheduled to be received by Government in 
March, 2004; and 
(b) if so, the outcome thereof and the recommendation in the Report 
received by Government alongwith the action taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRSAND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL DUTT): (a) 
and (b) Yes, Sir. A National Commi ssion for Youth was set up by the 
Government in March 2002. The Commission submitted the Executive 
Summary of the Report to the Government on 7th February, 2004 and was to 
submit its Report by March, 2004. As the Commission required more time for 
detailed examination of the many reports of the research studies the result of 
which may have a significant bearing on its Report, its tenure was extended 
beyond 31st March, 2004. The Commission finally submitted its Report to the 
Government on 16th July, 2004. The major recommendations of the Commission 
include creation of a Central Authority, merger of various youth related schemes, 
creation of a new Statutory Body at national level, establishment of an Inter-
Departmental Committee on Youth Affairs, setting up of a National Bank for 
Youth, making Skill and Vocational training a part of the curricula in schools from 
middle level and recommendations for youth of North Eastern Region. The 
Report and recommendations of the Commission are being examined by the 
Government.

Implementation of National Youth Policy, 2003 
† 2371. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government after adopting the National Youth 
Policy, 2003, have started implementing the same in order to make youth of the 
country actively participate in National Development as also to inspire them; 
and 
(b) if so, the primary areas, activities and priorities of the policy alongwith the 
mode of its implementation in Bihar including other States and the amount 
spent on this so far alongwith the results thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Government have adopted the National Youth Policy, 
2003 for all-round development of the youth. The Policy has also streesed the 
need to involve the youth in various programmes and activities for National 
development. 
The Policy has recognised four thrust areas i.e. Youth Empowerment; Gender 
Justice; Inter-Sectoral Approach; and Information and Research Network; 
It has identified the following areas as Key Sectors of concern for the 
youth:— 
(a) Education; (b) Training and Employment; (c) Health and Family 
Welfare; (d) Preservation of Environment, Ecology and Wild life; (e) 
Recreation and Sports; (f) Arts and Culture; (g) Science and Technology; and (h) 
Civics and Good Citizenship. 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
171 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
It also accorded priority to the following groups of young people:— 
(i) Rural and Tribal Youth; (ii) Out-of-School Youth; (iii) Adolescents 
particularly female adolescents; (iv) Youth with disabilities; and (v) Youth under 
specially difficult circumstances like victims of trafficking; orphans and street 
children. 
There is no State-wise allocation of funds for implemetation of the Policy. 
An Implementation Mechanism has been included in the Policy through which 
various youth development programmes and activities are to be undertaken 
with active involvement of State Government and Union Ministries and 
Departments.

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
Programmes for promotion of sports amongst weaker sections 
†2378. SHRI NARAYAN SINGH KESRI: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the programmes being run by Government to promote sports 
amongst young men/women and students of Scheduled Castes and weaker 
sections; 
(b) whether any programme is being operated by Government to bring the 
young men/women of Scheduled Caste Community in the mainstream; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the role of 'Nehru Youth Centre' in this direction? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) to (c) All the sports promotion programmes of the Ministry are 
implemented through general schemes. There is no such scheme specifically 
meant for Scheduled Castes and weaker sections. However, Sports Authority of 
India (SAI) through its schemes like National Sports Talent contest Scheme 
(NSTC) and Special Area Games Centre (SAG) cater specifically to induct 
talent from the remote, backward, tribal, coastal, hilly regions of the country 
and provide them sports training along with other sections of the community. 
(d) Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) is implementing two types of 
programmes through its district level kendras, which are promoting sports 
amongst all sections of youth including scheduled castes and weaker sections. The 
details of the above two programmes are as under: 
Sports Promotion Programmes 
The main objective of the Programme is to promote sports culture and 
sportsmanship among rural youth and to improve sports scenario in rural areas. It 
also aims at popularizing rural sports and games which require minimum 
infrastructure, equipment and finance. Each NYK has to organize three Sports 
Promotion Programmes and a sum of Rs.5000/- is allotted to each programme. 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
180 

[25 August. 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
Rural Sports Clubs 
The principal objective of this scheme is to help the emergence of a countrywide 
network of Sports Club Culture for channelizing the energies of youth for constructive 
activities on one hand and exploring and nurturing sports talent in rural and tribal areas on 
the others. Funds to the tune of Rs.30,000/- (normal area) and Rs.45,000/- (tribal area) are 
earmarked for each such club. NYKS has been entrusted with the responsibility to 
implement this scheme. 
Gradation of cricketers 
2379. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that BCCI has decided to grade cricket players in three 
categories in the matter of salaries; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the cricket players are not happy about the gradation and 
also about the reduction of match fee; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps Government propose to take in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL DUTT): (a) 
and (b) As per information received from the Board of Control for cricket in India 
(BCCI), BCCI would be entering into a yearly contract with maximum of 20 leading 
cricketers of the country and the retainership would be paid in three categories on the 
basis of their performances. This would be in addition to regular match fees and daily 
allowances. 
(c) and (d) The BCCI has also informed that the matter pertaining to gradation of 
cricketers based on performance is under discussion with the players and there is no 
reduction in the match fees of the players. BCCI does not have any report about any 
player being unhappy over the proposed contract system. 
(e) The issues relates entirely to the internal functioning of the BCCI, an autonomous 
body. The Government has no role in this regard.

MOTION UNDER RULE 267 TO SUSPEND QUESTION HOUR 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): Hon. Chairman, Sir, with your kind permission, I beg to 
move the following Motion: 
"That in pursuance of Rule 267 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of 
Business in the Rajya Sabha, this House do suspend Rule 38 of the said rule in 
its application in order to take up consideration and return of the 
Appropriation (No. 3) Bill, 2004 as passed by the Lok Sabha." 
The question was proposed. 
SHRI FALIS. NARIMAN (Nominated): Mr. Chairman, Sir, I oppose the Motion 
for suspension of Question Hour because it sets a very wrong and dangerous precedent, 
namely, that major political parties can by agreement effectively prevent this 
House from functioning. The suspension of the important business of Question Hour 
is only because one section of the House does not desire that the business of the House 
should go on at all unless satisfactory answers are given to three points that have been 
raised. But it appears to be willing that the Budget be passed, but only if it is without 
discussion. This infringes, Sir, upon the rights of the individual Members under Rule 
182. There are nearly 70 Members who are either Independent or nominated or belonging 
to small parties, and their rights as Members are being denied merely because leaders of 
some major political parties on both sides of the House are agreeable to a totally 
undemocratic procedure. Sir, we have a large number of questions on the Budget 
which we are entitled to discuss under Rule 182 and there are a large number of 
clarifications to be sought from the Finance Minister. Ever since this Session started in 
May this 
1

RAJYA SABHA [26 August, 2004] 
year, there has been no meaningful discussion on any matter, not even on the 
President's Address. All this, Sir, I submit, has gravely imperilled the future of 
our system of Parliamentary democracy. I wish to register my protest to this 
mode of proceeding and I, therefore, oppose this Motion. 
SHRI BIMAL JALAN (Nominated): Mr. Chairman, Sir, humbly and 
with a great deal of sadness, I have rise n to say that in any case this particular 
Motion should not be passed by a voice vote. If there is any agreement among 
the major parties—I know it is going to be passed— but, some of us, who feel 
strongly against the kind of procedure,  which has been adopted, should be 
allowed to register our dissent. Therefore, my suggestion, Mr. Chairman, as you 
are in the Chair, is that we should take a vote on the Motion even if there are 
only one or two of us who dissent. At least, the public has a right to know. I have 
the highest regard, Sir, for both the sides. Some of them are present and some of 
them are not present. I also abide by the agreement among the major parties. 
After all, it is a oarty-based Parliame ntary democracy. But the voice of some 
of us who belong to none of the parties should also be heard on important 
matters like this. On matters, which in my view, are not in the public interest, 
which are not in line with the Constitution and which are not in line with the 
Parliamentary traditions, at least, our dissent, even if it is by one Member, should 
be recorded that it is not a unanimous decision of this Council of States. So, my 
request to you, Mr. Chairman, is that you take not a voice vote but put this 
particular Motion to a ballot, even if there is only one dissent. At least, the 
public would know that it is not unanimous. Thank you very much. 
SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI (Maharashtra): Sir, there are two 
Motions, one is regarding the suspension of the Question Hour and the other is 
passing the Budget without discussion. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: That is not here at the moment. 
SHRI SHARAD ANANTRAO JOSHI: I oppose the idea of suspending 
Question Hour because there are some very important questions in the list 
today. I think, the passing of the Budget can be done after Question Hour. 
Thank you.

opportunity to present before you the genuine grievance of those who are 
labelled as Independents. It is two years I have been in this House.

When I came here in July 2002, for nearly thirteen to fourteen days the House 
had been witnessing a very serious state of pandemonium. At that time, the 
present ruling party was in the Oppos ition benches and it was impossible for 
the House to carry on normal business. Now, the tables have been turned and 
those who were in the Government are now in the Opposition. They enter into 
agreements without consulting us who are Independents. At least, consultation 
with one or two of us would have helped to present our views to them. On the

others.

is based on the incidence of poverty as per the 1993-94 adjusted shares of 
poverty. During 2004-05 a Central allocation of Rs.283.09 cr. has been made 
under Sampoorna Grameen Ro2gar Yojana (SGRY), Rs.60.08 cr. 
under Swamjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) and Rs. 107.31 cr. under 
Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY). Since inception of the scheme upto 
31.03.2004 the number of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) formed in the State is 
2.58 lakh which are at different stages of evolution. 
2. Golden Quadrilateral and Rural Roads 
On account of the geographical location of the State of Madhya Pradesh, the 
Golden Quadrilateral does not pass through Madhya Pradesh as the 
shortest National Highways connecting the above metros do not pass 
through Madhya Pradesh. However, substantial length of North-South 
and

total length under North-South and East-West corridors in MP is

Madhya Pradesh for the years 2000-01 to 2004-05 is Rs.2089.72 
crore. Against this, an amount of Rs. 1206.93 crore has already been 
released. The annual allocation for Madhya Pradesh is Rs.213

Programme (APDRP), 39 projects costing Rs.679.08 crores were

crores have already been released as first tranche. An amount of

for further release of funds, MPSEB should utilize at least Rs.170 
crores i.e. Rs.84.87 crores from APDRP and equal amount of 
counter-part funds. The State Government also needs to take 
effective steps to implement power sector reforms/improvements 
to be effected by Government of Madhya Pradesh as per MoA 
signed by Government of Madhya Pradesh with Government of 
India. 
As regards incentive claim under APDRP for the financial year 2002-
03, Madhya Pradesh State Elect ricity Board has submitted a 
proposal for grant of Rs.699.28 crores as incentive. The proposal 
for incentive claim is being examined by the Ministry of Power. 
Regarding losses suffered by Madhya Pradesh State in the power 
sector due to the division of the State, it is pointed out that a 
formal division of assets and liabilities between Madhya Pradesh 
State Electricity Board and Chhattisgarh State Electricity Board is still 
pending. Therefore, no compensation is due to Madhya Pradesh

cover 
Though the recorded forests in the State are 30% of its area, the 
forest cover is 25.07%. The benefit of forests in maintaining the soil 
and water regime of the State are supplemented in providing 
sustenance to the forest fringe dwellers. Madhya Pradesh has 
sizeable rural and tribal population who depend on the forests for 
livelihood. The issue of compensation to States for conservation 
of forest cover is a policy matter with wide ramifications. A view 
cannot be taken in isolation for any one State.

As far as coal mining is concerned, the Department of Coal has 
introduced a Bill, namely the Coal Mi nes (Nationalisation) Amendment Bill, 
2000 in the Rajya Sabha on 24.4.2004 to amend the Coal Mines 
(Nationalisation) Act, 1973. This Bill seeks to allow commercial mining of coal 
any Indian company both in public sector  and private sector. At present coal 
mining in India is allowed to Indian companies under the existing provisions 
of law. Under the Coal Mines (Notionalisation) Act, 1973 coal mining is 
exclusively reserved for the public s ector. By an amendm ent to the Act in 
1976, two exceptions to this policy were introduced viz. (i) captive mining by 
private companies engaged in production of iron and steel and (ii) sub-lease

steel. Mining of Coal for production of cement has also been permitted by the 
Government vide notification dated 15.3.96. 
(b) and (c) For non-fuel and non-atomic minerals, the above mentioned 
National Mineral Policy is equally applicable to all States in the country. In so 
far as coal is concerned, the State Government are allowed commercial 
mining of coal through their undertakings which are authorized by their Articles 
of Association to do mining of coal and lignite. Any Indian company can apply 
for working of coal reserve in any State for captive mining of coal for power 
generation, iron and steel production and cement production keeping into 
account the quality and quantity of coal reserve available in the State.

(d) A number of steps have been taken by the Government to fight cyber 
crimes. It is a coordinated effort on the part of several agencies in the Ministry of 
Home Affairs and in the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology 
on an on going basis. The fight against cyber crimes involves Law Enforcement 
Agencies such as the Central Bureau of Investigation, Intelligence Bureau, State 
Police organizations and other specialized organizations such as the National Police 
Academy and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-ln). 
CERT-ln has a role in developing appropriate Security Guidelines and other best 
practices to advise the Systems Administrators of computer systems and networks all 
over the country to implement them so as to avoid the systems from being attacked 
by the hackers and other criminals. In the event of systems being attacked, CERT-ln 
helps the victim organizations recover their systems from the computer security 
incidents so as to make them operational at the earliest. Cyber Forensics is an 
emerging discipline which helps the Law Enforcement organizations collect evidence 
from the scene of crime. The legal framework for fighting cyber crimes is a part of 
the Information Technology Act, 2000. Central Bureau of investigation and other 
police organizations have set up Cyber Crime Cells with police officers who have 
been specially trained in cyber forensics and also on IT security matters.

Victimization of office bearers of SC/ST employees association 
2417. SHRIVIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of COMMUNICA

SC/ST Employees Welfare Association are being victimized as they are

grievances;

representative of MTNL SC/ST Employees Association. Both have expressed 
their grievances to get facilities on the plea that they are the actual 
representatives of association of SC/ST employees. The matter stands referred 
to National Commission for SC/ST for guidance by MTNL.

Green Card Scheme 
2419. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister 
of COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Germany has extended Green Card Scheme 
for Overseas Information Technology specialists to work in Germany; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any limit has been prescribed for issue of work permits under 
the Green Card Scheme; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. 
SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The German Federal Cabinet approved the extension of the so-called 
"Green Card initiative" for foreign IT specialists. First time applications can 
be submitted until 31st December, 2004. The new imigration law passed by 
the German Parliament on 9th July, 2004, aims at attracting skilled workers into 
Germany including in knowledge based areas and provides for the possibility 
of offering permanent residence status  to highly qualified specialists and 
foreign university graduates. 
(c) and (d) There is no prescribed time limit for issue of worK permits under 
the Green Card Scheme. However, the new regulation cancels the earlier fixed 
maximum limit of 20,000 work permits.

Statement 
List of major recommendations of TRAI on broadband 
1. To promote quick growth and create immediate competition in 
broadband services, non-discriminatory Local Loop Unbundling 
(LLU) should be executed in a time bound manner for both Shared 
Unbundling and Bit Stream Access. The owner of the local loop who 
is a unified access or basic services access provider (LL 
Operator) will have the opportunity to decide in which exchanges 
they want to make the investment to upgrade the infrastructure for 
their own use as well as for prov iding Bit Stream Access to access 
seekers. A list of such exchanges should be specified by the LL 
Operator for Bit Stream Access, with the expected date by which 
the facility would be provided. This list should be provided 
within one month of implementation of the LLU programme. 
This information should be available in the public domain and 
regularly updated. 
86 

[26 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
2. The Authority will undertake the LLU programme in a time-bound 
phased manner, with each phase  being 3 months. For those 
exchanges in which the LL operators choose not to provide Bit 
Stream Access (or are unable to provide) in the first phase of the LLU 
programme, LL Operators should be mandated to provide Shared 
Unbundling and collocation facilities. The Authority will review the 
implementation during each phase and take action as appropriate to 
achieve the objectives. 
3. The Authority expects that LL Operators would most likely find it 
easier to focus on extending broadband services through their own 
efforts or their franchises. The Authority is of the view that for 
introduction of a competitive stimulus, it is also important to have 
non-discriminatory access by others to the above-mentioned unbundled 
local loop of LL Operators. The Authority would monitor the 
development in this regard, and expects that such opportunities 
would be provided by LL Operators to steadily increase the presence 
of non-franchisee access seekers during each of the phases mentioned 
above. 
4. To continue to promote roll-out of new broadband-capable 
infrastructure, LLU will be implemented only for lines that are five 
years old from 2004-05, the fiscal year of implementation of the LLU 
programme. The same principle shall apply for all installations in the 
future once they complete five years. Therefore, all installations that 
were completed before the 1999-2000 fiscal year w ill be subject to 
LLU, and at the end of the 2004-05 fi scal year, lines installed during 
1999-2000 will be subject to LLU rules. LL Operators will be 
required to submit to the Authority within 2 days of the date of issue 
of these recommendations a complete list of all lines and their 
associated year of installation into service. This will be used for 
public reference in implementing the LLU programme. In the event that 
identifying the installation date of lines presents a problem in 
achieving the goals of the LLU programme, the effective date for 
unbundled lines can be shifted to a later date. These parameters will be 
revisited in the future as the Authority performs its regular reviews on 
the progress of achieving the goals of the LLU programme.

5. An Open Sky policy should be adopted for VSAT operators, similar to 
what is available to ISPs and broadcasters. VSAT service providers 
should be allowed to work directly with any international satellite.

removed to allow operators further cost savings and increased 
operational efficiencies by taking advantage of available 
technologies. Additionally, throughout restrictions on VSAT 
services, for both uplink to the satellite and downlink to remote-
stations, should be completely removed. SACFA clearance should

connection with a PSTN exchange/PLMN network for inter-

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) to (e) Bilateral discussions on a 
number of subjects have been held between India and Pakistan within the 
framework of the Composite Dialogue. President Musharraf s reassurance in the 
Joint Press Statement of January 6,2004, not to permit any territory under 
Pakistan's control to be used to support terrorism in any manner, allowed the 
process of the Composite Dialogue to be initiated in February 2004. An agreed 
schedule of meetings was worked out during the Foreign Secretary level talks 
between India and Pakistan on 18 February, 2004. Accordingly, meetings were

communication links between the two DGMOs, establish a hotline between 
Foreign Secretaries and to work toward s MoU on pre-notification of flight 
testing of missiles. The Foreign Secretaries of the two countries met in New 
Delhi on June 27-28, 2004 and discussed "Peace and Security including 
CBMs" and "Jammu and Kashmir", within the framework of the Composite 
Dialogue. The two sides proposed a comprehensive framework for CBMs aimed 
at initiating and

views on carrying the process forward in an atmosphere free from terrorism

Commercial Cooperation, Terrorism and Drug Trafficking, and Promotion of 
Friendly Exchanges in various fields, were held in the last week of July and 
first half of August, and views were exchanged on these issues. During 
discussions on Promotion of Friendly Exchanges in various fields, wide-
ranging proposals were made for promoting friendly exchanges and 
cooperation in the fields of art, cultu re, archaeology, education, science and 
technology, youth affairs and sports, media and tourism. India also made a 
series of proposals for trade promotion, transit, cooperation in the fields of 
agriculture, petroleum and natural gas, banking, information technology, 
telecommunications, postal services, civil aviation, shipping, capital market, 
etc. between the two countries. A meeting between the Foreign Ministers of 
the two countries, to review the overall progress, is scheduled to be held in 
India on September 5-6, 2004. It would be preceded by a meeting between 
the Foreign Secretaries on September 4, 2004.

Official policy to deal with hostage situation 
2447. SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHAR YA: Will the Minister of 
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have in place any set official policy to deal with 
the hostage situation by domestic and foreign terrorists; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) whether there is any proposal to formulate basic guidelines to deal 
the cases of hostages which of late, have started increasing and if not, the 
reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) to (d) It is the policy of the 
Government of India not to compromise with terrorist groups or elements. 
However, while adhering to this principle, the objective of the Government is to 
ensure the safety and well-being of all its citizens, whether in India or abroad. 
In case of hostage-taking, Governments makes all efforts possible to secure 
the early and safe release of its nationals. In order to deal with hostage 
situations, the Government has an institutionalised mechanism in place. There 
is a crisis management group which is set up immediately and is tasked with the 
constant monitoring and handling of the situation in close consultation with 
concerned agencies, our diplomatic missions abroad and with foreign 
governments. The Cabinet Secretary also holds a parallel set of inter-ministerial 
meetings, as required, to take appropriate decisions. The Cabinet Committee 
on Political Affairs may 
112 

[26 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
also meet, as necessary, to review the situation and take appropriate decisions. 
This mechanism remains in force until the crisis ends. It needs to be pointed out 
that no two hostage situations are entirely similar and different responses may 
be required depending upon specific circ umstances to reach the objectives of 
Government policy.

Norms for U.S. citizenship 
2449. SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA: Will the Minister of 
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the U.S. Administration has set very rigorous norms for the 
immigrants who intend to adopt the U.S. citizenship;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) and (b) The rules for

i.  must be 18 years of age; 
113

ii. must be lawfully admitted to the US for permanent residence and possess an

BIMSTEC Summit 
2450. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SA NGHI: Will the Minister of 
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the benefits derived by India in the recently held BIMSTEC 
Summit in Bangkok; 
(b) whether any Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) has been signed in the Summit; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) in what manner would it help the Indian industry? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) The Prime Minister attended the First Bay of Bengal 
Initiative for Multh-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Sumit in 
Bangkok on 31 July, 2004. The Summit identified six priority sectors of cooperation, each 
with a "lead country": technology (Sri Lanka), transport and communications (India), 
energy (Myanmar), tourism (India) and fisheries (Thailand). Increased 
cooperation in these sectors among the BIMSTEC member countries would benefit ail 
the member countries. BIMSTEC provides an effective (ink between South Asia and 
Southeast Asia with significant potential for deeper economic interaction and integration. 
It also provides us with a 
114 

[26 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
sub-regional frame work for the development, in particular of the eastern and 
northeastern regions of India. All the leaders unanimously agreed on the need to 
cooperate in combating international terrorism and important step in this 
direction is the setting up of the BIMSTEC Joint Working Group on 
Counter-Terrorism. 
(b) and (c) No such agreement wa s signed at Summit. However, the 
BIMSTEC Framework Agreement on Free Trade Area was singed during the 
Sixth Ministerial Meeting in Phuket, Thailand in February, 2004 by Bhutan, 
India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Bangladesh joined the 
Agreement in June, 2004. The Framework Agreement provides a roadmap for 
Free Trade Area Agreements in goods, services, investment and other areas of 
general economic cooperation. The nego tiations on FTA in goods are to be 
begin in September, 2004 and to be concluded by December 2005. The 
negotiations on FTA in services and investment shall commence in 2005 and 
be concluded by 2007. 
(d) The Framework Agreement aims at strengthening and enhancing 
cooperation in economic, trade and investment among the parties through the 
progressive liberalization and promotion of trade in goods, services and 
investment.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) Yes. 
(b) The Declaration welcomes the signing of the Framework

towards a Free Trade Area with the objective of eventually arriving at a South 
Asian Economic Union.

The Declaration emphasizes the imoprtance of cooperation in energy, 
transportation and communication links in promoting accelerated and balanced 
economic growth issues. The Declaration refers to, inter alia, cooperation on

environment, and information and communication technology. The 
Declaration also underscores the importance of poverty alleviation and the 
need for investment in human resources and skills development. 
Hailing the signature of SAARC Social Charter, the Declaration notes the far-

RAJYA SABHA [26 August, 2004] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) and (b) Yes. Sir. The Tenth Five Year 
Plan, as approved by the National Deve lopment Council, recognises that in 
order to increase the rate of growth of GDP to 8 per cent over the Tenth Five Year 
Plan period and to attain specified monitorable targets, the overall investment rate 
of the economy will have to increase to 28.4 per cent of GDP for the Tenth Plan
